sentences.text: Along with the main appeal I.A.No.1/2020 is filed to condone the delay of 1167 days i.e. nearly three and half years, in filing the appeal.

3. On going through the affidavit filed in support of the application, it is contended that, due to ill-health of her father she could not contact her counsel immediately after the disposal of the case and later her husband died; she was in financial difficulties and thus, there is a delay of 1167 days in filing the appeal.
4. Learned counsel for the respondent-Insurance company filed objections to the I.A. seeking condonation and contended that, the delay is abnormal and it has not been explained properly.
The delay has occurred much earlier to the death of the husband of the claimant No.(a) and there are no sufficient or bonafide reasons to condone the delay.
Therefore, requested to dismiss the appeal.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:7468 HC-KAR 5.
Sri. Shaik Khaleel Ahmed, the deceased i.e. husband of the claimant No.(a) met with accident on 18.12.2014 and the claim petition was filed in the year 2016.
It came to be disposed of on 22.09.2016.
The deceased Shaik Khaleel Ahmed died on 29.11.2018 i.e. after two years of the disposal of the petition.
Claimant No.(a) filed this appeal in the year 2020.
Hence, there is a huge delay in filing the appeal.
6. The deceased Shaikh Khaleel Ahmed survived for two years after disposal of the case, but he has not taken any steps to file the appeal.
The claimant No.(a) has not filed any medical records of her father and the reasons stated by her is that she was under financial difficulties.
The reasons assigned in the affidavit cannot be accepted as she would have approached Legal Services Authority for free legal aid.
It appears that, the claimant No.(a) might have filed this appeal as a after thought to gain wrongfully.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:7468 HC-KAR 7.
The reasons assigned for the delay are neither convincing nor satisfactory.

Accordingly,
I.A.No.1/2020 is dismissed.
Consequently, the appeal is also dismissed.
